column1: # .github/npm-audit-register.tsv — the reviewed record of every npm advisory
# accepted against ui/package-lock.json.
# Policy, gate rules and the reasoning behind this file's shape:
#   scripts/npm-audit.sh
# See the current picture with: scripts/npm-audit.sh --report
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   advisory  GHSA id, e.g. GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx (identity — one row each)
#   package   the vulnerable package
#   severity  as reported by npm audit; context only, refreshed by eye
#   scope     runtime | dev — which tree it lands in with --omit=dev
#   reason    REQUIRED. Why this is accepted, and what would unblock it.
#   issue     REQUIRED. The issue tracking the eventual fix.
# A row here suppresses a HIGH or CRITICAL advisory that would otherwise fail
# the build. It is not a place to record that something is unimportant — the
# only justification is that a fix is not shippable YET (no upstream release,
# the fix is in a major version that needs validation, a transitive pin we do
# not control). "We looked and it's fine" is not a reason to add a row; it is
# a reason to leave the advisory unregistered and let it be fixed.
# Moderate, low and info advisories are reported on every run and never
# blocked, so they do not belong here either.
# There is no --refresh that generates these rows, deliberately. Each one is
# written by hand by someone who read the advisory. The gate rejects a row
# with an empty reason or no issue.
# Currently EMPTY, and not as a placeholder: on 2026-08-31, the run that
# introduced this gate, `npm audit` reported ZERO advisories at every severity
# across all 447 packages (25 prod, 386 dev, 87 optional). The gate landed
# green with nothing suppressed. If this file is still empty, that is the
# state being asserted — no exceptions have ever been needed.
advisory
